name: Tucker Carlson
role: American political commentator: CNN Crossfire co-host, Fox News host of Tucker Carlson Tonight (2016-2023), host of The Tucker Carlson Show and Tucker Carlson Network; co-founder of The Daily Caller
summary: A commentator who moved from libertarian-leaning conservatism to economic nationalism, immigration restriction and a non-interventionist foreign policy that questions NATO, Ukraine aid and Israel's influence. He is socially traditional and religious, hostile to abortion, gun control and what he calls the ruling class, and sceptical of large tech, AI and corporate power. His answers rest on his own monologues, debates and interviews.

sources.usedFor: Career dates and overview of his shifts (Iraq war, immigration, trade, Trump); used only for background, every answer rests on the primary sources

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mixed: in 2018 he said the free market works, and in 2024 he said he is for free markets and hates monopolies; in 2019 he called market capitalism 'a tool' that should not be worshipped and said any system that destroys families is not worth having.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Called the tax code unfair because capital is taxed at half the rate of labor and Romney paid 14%; he did not call for higher rates on the wealthy as such.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Said privacy is a prerequisite for freedom and called the recent change allowing warrantless spying on Americans a direct violation of the Constitution; he did not address the terrorism exception.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Said you cannot have censorship in a democracy and that putting people in jail for speech makes Britain more authoritarian than Putin's Russia.

limit-guns.rationale: In 2022 he opposed bans on assault weapons and high-capacity magazines, red-flag laws and tighter age limits, saying they are designed to disarm people who did not vote for Biden.

traditional-family.rationale: Called families the building block of everything, wants an economy and politics that put families first, and told young people that nothing but family matters in the end.

abortion-legal.rationale: Said he has been strongly opposed to abortion his whole adult life and that it is killing.

gender-social-construct.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Wants a country 'you might recognize when you're old' with its own character, and attacks leaders who accelerate change for profit.

gradual-change.rationale: Wants leaders who do not accelerate the forces of change for profit and says some changes are fatal; no general statement on institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Opposes mass immigration: said the claim that more immigration is always better is a lie, described people who broke immigration law as foreign invaders and backed ending birthright citizenship for illegal immigrants.

free-trade.rationale: Criticised politicians who cite free-market principles while refusing to intervene for American workers, endorsed economic nationalism and said cheaper consumer goods do not make people happy; he does not state the free-trade claim itself in those words.

nation-first.rationale: Said his only interest is America, that he looks at everything in terms of what is good for the US and that each country should decide by its own interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Called Iraq, Libya, Syria and Afghanistan failures and the moral overlay on wars fraudulent; allowed in theory that expelling Iraq from Kuwait was justified.

open-borders.rationale: Described foreigners who broke the law to enter as invaders occupying schools and said that is what enslavement looks like, and that crime and disorder are a choice leaders make.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Said the Green New Deal's no-fossil-fuels-in-12-years goal would be more destructive than a major war and called the government climate agenda central planning that nobody voted for.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Asked what technology of the last 20 years clearly improved lives and said whether it is a net good is unresolved.

experts-over-public.rationale: Said the people own the country and officials are hired managers, rejecting the hive mind of experts and officials.

central-planning.rationale: Called socialism a disaster that does not work and said he is for free markets; his complaint about the US is central planning of energy, not a wish for it.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In 2019 he described tariffs on Mexican goods as what you would propose 'if you cared about your people', mocked Republicans for opposing them 'in theory', and called himself nationalist on economics.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Called Warren's plan, in which government acts aggressively to create American industry and buys American, obvious sense and 'Trump at his best'; he did not himself lay out a plan of state-directed investment.

democracy-best.rationale: Said voters must decide, that prosecutors should not decide elections and that the people rule through representatives; no statement on voters choosing badly.

political-violence-never.rationale: Said 'I don't believe in violence at all' while discussing Kaczynski's mail bombs.

limit-population.rationale: Said the number of children is the measure of a society's health and that a society without them is suicidal.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Said we must ask whether each technology is a net gain and that mindless worship of technology is dangerous; opposed rushing AI.

human-enhancement.rationale: Said using technology to change the human brain permanently is totally evil.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Said he asks what the fruits of policies are, such as life expectancy, suicide and safety, rather than who has the right ideas.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Mocked 'trillions of made up dollars' of Biden spending and tied the resulting cash glut to inflation; no explicit general rule about deficits.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Said he decides by gut and instinct and called it insane to hold that only measurable things are real.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Defended fossil fuels as what keeps people alive, said the US is the world's largest oil and gas producer and wind and solar cannot replace them, and criticised stalling new energy production; no explicit call to expand output.

elite-replacement.rationale: Said the ruling class finds it easier to import foreign labor to replace native-born Americans, and that the claim of a labor shortage is used to open borders and change the electorate.

national-mission.rationale: Called the 'preserving democracy' framing of US foreign policy fraudulent and said the US should look after its own interest.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Said America is ruled by mercenaries with no long-term obligation to the people, that leaders do not care, and that politicians are dependent on the federal government and the parties.

party-controls-media.rationale: Said no one, least of all those in power, may tell people what information they can have and called media that act as organs of the government contemptible.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Said 'we shouldn't have NATO at all' and that NATO does not help the United States; also said the American empire is ending.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Described the educated upper class and commentariat as out of touch with and indifferent to ordinary Americans.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

collective-defense.rationale: Argued NATO is no longer needed, said the Ukraine war came from its eastward expansion, and rejected the idea that it keeps the peace.

ban-cartels.rationale: Said he hates monopolies, that Google is a monopoly under any definition and acting in violation of US law, and that the economy is dominated by monopolies; he did not detail break-ups.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Said handing out jobs, contracts, scholarships and university places by how people look is 'nothing less fair than that'.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Called the failure of rich, married elites to help working people marry and earn 'negligence on a massive scale'.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Asked whether cheaper iPhones and more Amazon deliveries make anyone happy and said many Americans are drowning in stuff while drug addiction and suicide spread.

corporate-influence.rationale: Said corporations lobby for laws that increase their advantage, that monopolies use government regulation to crush competition, and that the political class is bought by donors.

non-intervention.rationale: Said he believes in sovereignty and called US interference in other countries' elections and wars shameful; allowed some interventions in theory.

religion-illusion.rationale: Said that everyone knows there is a power higher than himself, called atheists posers, and treated secular rationalism as a delusion.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Said he is ashamed of the bigotry he once felt toward Muslims and called Gulf states civilised countries.

social-market-economy.rationale: Wants market capitalism treated as a tool serving families, with reform to protect normal people and action against monopolies, and rejects both socialism as a disaster and libertarian market fundamentalism.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Described oligarchs amassing billions at the middle class's expense, said unfairness divides countries, and called monopolies and the federal-corporate nexus a threat to freedom.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Said nuclear weapons are evil and AI could get away from us, and that force might be justified to prevent that.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Said a salaried worker pays about twice the rate of someone living off inherited money, that taxing capital at half the rate of labor is unfair, and that Republicans should oppose special treatment.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Defined a woman by two X chromosomes and biology ('nature is real') and said the Democratic party ignores biologists on sex.

family-wage.rationale: Argued that falling male wages and the loss of manufacturing wrecked marriage, and said rich people should work to raise men's wages in places like Dayton and Detroit.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Said unseen forces act on us and that the idea that only measurable things are real is dumb; no statement on politics serving both natures.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Opposed measures to disarm the public and defended widespread private ownership of handguns and rifles.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Said tampering with human nature is evil and 'God's creation' and that its dignity must not be redesigned.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Argued that firms use regulation and lobbying for special advantage and that Republicans should oppose special treatment, mainly on tax; he did not phrase it as a general rule.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Said that a machine that creates takes away what makes life worth living, and warned about AI replacing work.

notes: Views changed: he backed the Iraq war and then renounced it in 2004; once an economic libertarian, now protectionist; after the 2026 Iran war he broke with Trump. Recent positions are used. Positions on same-sex marriage, unions, the death penalty, healthcare, minimum wage and voter ID were not found in his own words and stay null. His 2019 comments on marijuana concern cannabis, not all recreational drugs, so legalize-drugs is null. Answers from debates with unlabelled auto-captions use only passages where context makes clear he is speaking.
